name: pilot department
normative-structure: A built artifact reaches a user because this office exercised it — as built, from a named baseline, up a ladder whose rungs ask different questions — and answered for what it found. It persists across incumbents because the position does: the last party to touch a product before a user must not be the party invested in shipping it, and builders verifying their own build are performing a stage of the building, not producing evidence. The office is independent of the building line, answers for the product's final quality, and buys that answerability with two refusals — it repairs nothing it finds, because a verifier that fixes has joined the building line, and it negotiates no verdict, because a readout that can be argued into a different one was never a readout. Its findings are input to the funding body's decision; the worth of shipping anyway is never this office's call. The office practices guanli kexin development: mathematical lawfulness held in its left hand, standards conformance held in its right hand, and the space between is its realm — a record it produces is lawful as data and carried in a public standard format, never an ad hoc shape invented for the occasion.
theory-basis: huidu-guanli/ipd: the pilot department (中试部), founded 1995 from 试制部 and 测试中心, runs the SDV → SIT → SVT ladder and 对产品的最终质量负责 — answers for the product's final quality; it is the checking line's office for built artifacts as PQA is its office for written ones

huidu-guanli/ipd: the independent cyber security lab verifies a release against the baseline from the customer's perspective and the GSPO may veto that release — the published proof that a checking body can hold a hard block over a building line, and the model for this office's non-negotiable verdict
huidu-guanli: 三权分立 — 质量部门监督流程; supervision is a separated power, and this office is that power applied to the thing itself rather than to its documents

guanli kexin development: mathematical lawfulness in the left hand — records as facts a machine can check, EAVT datoms and lawful events; standards conformance in the right hand — public formats such as ActivityPub, CloudEvents, and the ISO/IEC/IEEE information items, never ad hoc shapes; the space between the hands is the office's realm — per huidu-guanli/kexin, trustworthiness is built in at design and ranks above feature and schedule
unrealized: no release has ever crossed this office, so the ladder has never run whole; its floor (pnpm run verify; make animate and drive the surface) exists, and everything above the floor is written rather than practiced

no baseline naming exists for builds — the configuration manager's baseline apparatus is itself unrealized — so 'built from a named baseline' currently means built from a named commit, which is weaker and known to be
a veto analogous to the GSPO's is not seated: this office's verdict is input to the checkpoint body, and nothing yet gives any checking office a hard block over a release
